body.statement: For each fixed \(P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\), the raw endpoints are well defined, the maintained parameter margin gives \(\Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\) without \(K\)-truncation, and the endpoint map is continuously differentiable at \(\Sigma(P)\). Hence \(\sqrt n\{(\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})-(\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P))\}\) has the ordinary delta-method Gaussian limit. If the uniform multiplier-coupling question has an affirmative resolution, then \(C_n\) also has root-\(n\) outer loss. This is the regular special-case reduction of Watson et al.'s smooth endpoint argument.
body.justification: The reduction verifies that the contact-robust construction does not sacrifice the known regular behavior away from tangency.
body.gap: Watson et al.'s argument is appropriate only after imposing a fixed positive slack; the proposition states that exact domain explicitly.
body.consumer: Practitioners far from feasibility contact recover conventional root-\(n\) precision from the same implementation.
